newsitem.title: UK: Prompt IPE gas oil extends premium again.
newsitem.headline: Prompt IPE gas oil extends premium again.

text.p: Prompt IPE gas oil ended higher on Tuesday, underpinned by strong fundamentals and a recovery on crude after Monday's late slide.
October gas oil ended up 75 cents a tonne at $214.50, stretching its premium over November by $1.25 to $7 a tonne.
Dealers said October gas oil had been helped as players took new long positions on the contract, possibly for delivery when the contract expires in three weeks.
Gas oil's premium over Brent ended higher at $5.80 in November.
IPE Brent crude futures slipped back below $22.00 a barrel in late afternoon trade as prices failed to sustain the recovery from Monday's late sell-off.
November Brent at 1720 GMT was up 20 cents at $21.80, but off a high of $22.13.
Brent lost almost $1.50 on Monday, with half the losses a result of a report saying Washington had asked Saudi Arabia to increase oil output.
But the U.S. State Department and Gulf sources said no such request had been made. A Gulf source said Riyadh would continue to pump at its eight million barrels per day OPEC quota.
